judged_by: Matched by a Claude Opus 5.5 agent on 2026-11-25; not yet checked by the labeler.

question.note: Spillover of the 'convicted criminal' ad onto perceptions of people with records (Q1), effect on sense of representation (Q3), and whether the counter-narrative mitigates it (Q2).

central_claim.note: Gives all three parts of C1: harm to perceptions, improved feelings of representation, counter-narrative 'largely mitigates' (paper: 'vastly ameliorated', 'almost entirely ameliorated').

evidence.note: E1 partial: survey experiment with self-identified U.S. Democrats, but no Prolific, dates or pre-registration in the claim. E2: total N and the three arms ('roughly evenly' level, as the earlier judge credited without arm counts; the counts are in the quotes). 'A Trump advertisement with a convicted criminal label' does not describe the mugshot stimulus, so no E3 credit.

key_findings.note: Keeps the order (before the ad) and the comparison with the ad alone; the quote gives >0.8 SD. Credited in full as the earlier judge did for a similar entry without the magnitude.

Both the representation increase and the public-service-motives increase, as in the earlier judge's full F3. 'Unexpectedly' fits: representation quality was not hypothesized and H2B predicted a decrease in motives.

scope_and_limits.note: Gives durability (with other contexts / less transparent designs, p.17); not repeated exposure or behavior.
Concern that AI agents completed the online survey (p.17).

theoretical_positioning.note: T1: social categorization, exemplar label spilling over to the group. T4 partial: 'applies' the theory to the Trump ad, but does not say it extends it or tests the predicted spillover.

interlocutor_claim.note: Ref. 54 (incarceration may shift ideology rightward) and the paper's doubt about it outside stigmatizing messaging (p.4): accurate, not a gold interlocutor.
